name: Baltic Sea
genZNote: The Baltic is one of the least salty seas on Earth — so many rivers pour fresh water in, and its exit to the ocean is so narrow, that it barely tastes like a sea at all.

sections.heading: 🌊 Location & Ocean Connection
bullets: A largely enclosed sea in Northern Europe, surrounded by the Scandinavian Peninsula and continental Northern/Eastern Europe.
Connects to the North Sea (and the wider Atlantic) through the narrow Danish straits.

sections.heading: 🗺️ Countries Bordering It
bullets: Sweden, Finland, Russia, Estonia, Latvia, Lithuania, Poland, Germany, and Denmark.

sections.heading: 🚢 Ports & Trade Routes
bullets: Major ports: Gdansk (Poland), Gothenburg (Sweden), Helsinki (Finland), St. Petersburg (Russia).
A key regional trade route for Northern and Eastern Europe, especially for timber, machinery and energy products.
Heavily used for regional ferry and short-sea shipping networks connecting Scandinavia to continental Europe.

sections.heading: 🐠 Economic & Ecological Significance
bullets: One of the least saline seas in the world because of heavy freshwater inflow from surrounding rivers and its narrow, shallow connection to the ocean.
Prone to seasonal oxygen-depletion ('dead zones') caused by nutrient runoff (eutrophication) from surrounding agricultural land.
Supported by strong regional cooperation (through bodies like HELCOM) aimed at reducing pollution and restoring its ecological health.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Baltic Sea is a largely enclosed, low-salinity sea in Northern Europe, connected to the North Sea only through the narrow Danish straits.
keyFacts: Borders Sweden, Finland, Russia, the Baltic states, Poland, Germany, Denmark.
One of the least saline seas due to heavy freshwater inflow.
Connects to the North Sea via the narrow Danish straits.
commonConfusion: The Baltic Sea and the North Sea are two different seas, connected only by narrow straits — not one continuous body.

highYieldFacts: Baltic Sea = low-salinity, largely enclosed sea in Northern Europe.
Connects to North Sea via the narrow Danish straits.
commonTraps: Don't assume the Baltic has ocean-typical salinity — it's notably less salty than most seas.
mustRemember: Baltic Sea = Northern Europe's low-salinity regional sea, narrow exit via Danish straits.

sources.name: HELCOM — Baltic Marine Environment Protection Commission
